subject: Remhir
evidence: Uploaded Blender source; 6,290,220 bytes; Blender header v2.77. Canonical Pose Lab archive intake pending binary/LFS commit.

subject: Remhir
evidence: Early gargoyle player character; infinite minimalist game; core remembered interaction punch, punch, counter; remembered as exceptionally fun and historically important in the shift away from sword-first combat.

subject: Gravity Fist Ares production history
evidence: AxeKick and Headbutt were fully authored; most other attacks began as mocap and were strengthened through key removal before later Pose Lab reduction.

subject: Remhir structural inspection
evidence: Main Body mesh has 2655 vertices / 2704 polys, 30-degree Edge Split, no subdivision modifier, Rigify metarig+rig, and 14 actions including Block, Counter, Parry, HeavyKick and three LightCombo actions. Wing controls dominate measured Block change and materially participate in Counter/Parry/combos.

subject: Remhir weapon-mode morphology
evidence: Body shape keys are Basis, HandMode, SwordMode. Recovered values HandMode=1, SwordMode=0. Driver expressions are HandMode=1-var*2 and SwordMode=var*2. HandMode changes 70 vertices and collapses long right-side blade geometry into the hand region; SwordMode changes 184 vertices around the hand/weapon relationship.

subject: Remhir style
evidence: Silhouette is dominated by enormous faceted bat wings over a narrow horned central body, enlarged upper legs, tapering lower legs and sparse spike punctuation. Hard planar topology carries the design more than surface detail in the surviving blend.

subject: material-channel A/B
evidence: On stylized low-poly assets, full PBR-style channel output versus diffuse-only was an A/B discontinuity: diffuse-only read as incomplete, not merely less polished. Candidate law: material channels can carry semantic object identity; stripping decorative surface noise must not be confused with stripping material truth.

subject: Remhir counter timing contract
evidence: Drew remembers Remhir's counter as fail-soft precision: the same defensive/counter attempt rewarded precise timing with a satisfying counter/reversal while an imperfect attempt degraded into a block rather than a full punish. He preferred this to his Dark Souls parry experience, where failed parry risk made attack-twice-then-block feel like a better proposition.

subject: Slime
evidence: Uploaded Blender 2.78 source; 899,920 bytes. Embedded history points to OneDrive Slime.blend and FBX export into hemomancy/Assets/Characters.

subject: Slime morphology
evidence: The rig is Root/RootBase/SlimeNeck/SlimeHead/RightPseudopod/LeftPseudopod/BackPseudopod. Outer slime shell and joined internal-bone composite share the same deformation-group vocabulary. The 342-vertex joined internal composite exactly matches the union of ten separate source bone meshes; distinct source pieces map wholly to RightPseudopod, LeftPseudopod, and BackPseudopod controls. Visible bones are therefore functional payloads carried by soft-body pseudopod regions, not passive support anatomy.

subject: Slime animation grammar
evidence: Five actions survive: 0T-Pose, Idle, SlimeAttack, SlimeDamaged, SlimeForward. SlimeAttack keys 0,15,19,21,23,24,26,28,35 with max local pseudopod translations ~1.151 back / 0.936 left / 0.846 right; scale channels remain 1.0, so attack deformation is translation/rotation + skinning rather than scale cheats.

subject: Slime shape-key discrepancy
evidence: Drew remembers Slime as possibly his most shape-key-heavy model, but this exact surviving blend contains zero Key datablocks and every mesh key pointer is null. Preserve both facts; earlier working revision, applied keys, or export-prep stripping are plausible but unproven.

subject: Slime visual intent
evidence: Drew describes a transparent slime body enclosing visible weapon-bones. Source verifies separately modeled slime and bone materials and an enclosing shell/internal-bone geometry relationship, but saved legacy material alpha reads 1.0; transparency remains intended/runtime memory rather than source-material proof in this revision.

subject: Lionheart aesthetic leverage
evidence: Drew judges Lionheart as better-looking than some AAA art despite materially lower-capability technology. The aesthetic comparison is subjective; source-measured support is Blender 2.80-era production, ~4,484 visible authored vertices / ~4,308 polygons including articulated flail geometry, disciplined semantic polygon allocation, and source-verified Substance Painter BaseColor export. Candidate law: visual quality is not monotonic with technical capability; strong silhouette and information allocation can outperform higher-budget rendering on taste/coherence dimensions.

subject: Vanguard source
evidence: Uploaded Blender 2.80 source; 10,454,904 bytes. Non-widget objects are Body, Long_Sword and rig. Embedded source path is OneDrive/Documents/Vanguard.blend and historical strings reference Modern Paladin/ArtSources/Vanguard.blend.

subject: Vanguard geometry and style
evidence: Body is 1032 verts / 910 polys, overwhelmingly quads and flat-shaded; Long_Sword is 321 verts / 288 polys. Body separates into 22 connected components including symmetric arm assemblies, a three-part custom right pauldron weighted to Pauldron.R, and ten 15-vertex head-weighted blade/feather strips forming the directional crest. Total visible authored geometry is only 1353 verts / 1198 polys.

subject: Vanguard animation grammar
evidence: 19 bAction datablocks survive. SwordAttack1 uses sparse semantic times 0,7,8,9,11,13,14,15,16,20,27,38 and root-Y moves from a +0.153 preload to -1.813 by frame 38. SwordAttack5 reaches -2.418. Root-driven travel makes the strikes whole-body commitments rather than stationary arm gestures.

subject: Vanguard Pose Lab sibling relation
evidence: The uploaded source shares Body/Long_Sword/rig and exact fcurve counts for all 19 common actions with the Pose Lab Vanguard import manifest. The Pose Lab sibling source/runtime has a twentieth SwordAttack3 action absent as a bAction datablock here, so treat this upload as a closely related source revision rather than byte-identical to the current imported copy.
